notes.title: Checked purity
notes.text: `pure` rules out effects such as I/O and clock access. The checker verifies it.

notes.title: Declared failure
notes.text: `try` declares that `mean` can fail. Its caller must handle the outcome.

notes.title: Bounded input
notes.text: `Int<0..1000>` carries a range. `ListView` gives read-only access.

notes.title: Visible propagation
notes.text: `total + r` is checked: an overflow is a failure, and `or fail` passes it to the caller.

notes.title: Changes declared once
notes.text: `let mut` says that `readings` will change, so the `push` that changes it needs no other marker.

notes.title: Caller’s recovery
notes.text: `catch` handles the failure, reports it and recovers with `0`.

notes.title: Authority as a parameter
notes.text: `main` declares the console it needs, and the runtime supplies it. Printing uses that capability.

notes.title: Cleanup belongs to the type
notes.text: `cleanup` runs exactly once, when a `Resource` is destroyed.

notes.title: Counted, explicit sharing
notes.text: `Shared[Console]` is reference-counted. `retain()` takes another reference, and says so.

notes.title: Destroyed in reverse order
notes.text: When `work` returns, `second` is destroyed before `first`, so the output reads `release 2` then `release 1`. No garbage collector decides when.

notes.title: Owned, then shared
notes.text: `main` owns the console it declares, and moves it into a `Shared` handle for the code it calls.

notes.title: Lent, not given away
notes.text: `work(console)` borrows the handle. `main` still owns it afterwards, and prints `done`.

notes.title: Ownership in the signature
notes.text: `owned Parcel` means `heavy` takes the parcel. The caller gives it up.

notes.title: Pure, and checked
notes.text: `pure`: no effects at all. The checker verifies the claim.

notes.title: Consume and take apart
notes.text: `match move p` consumes the parcel. The pattern binds the field it needs, and `_` discards the label.

notes.title: Destructuring a move
notes.text: `let Parcel(…) = move parcel` takes the fields out. `parcel` can't be used after this line.

notes.title: Fresh values need no marker
notes.text: A constructor's result is a fresh value, so it goes straight into `heavy` without `move`.

title: Recover, report or pass on
output:
0 4
half of 6 is 3
3 has no half

notes.title: Errors are declared
notes.text: An error has a stable code and a typed payload.

notes.title: Failing is in the signature
notes.text: `try` says `half` can fail, and `fail` is where it does.

notes.title: Recover in place
notes.text: `or recover 0` handles the failure on the spot.

notes.title: Or match on the outcome
notes.text: `match` sees success and failure as two explicit cases.

notes.title: Nothing is lost
notes.text: `report f` records the failure before carrying on with a value.

notes.title: Recovery is visible
notes.text: `recovers` is transitive: a function that absorbs a failure says so, and so does every function that reaches one, up to `main`.
